what_it_does: Digital power amplifiers for WiFi and cellular must transmit high power (27.7 decibel-milliwatts) with high efficiency (37.8 percent) and minimal distortion using switched-capacitor techniques. Switched-capacitor power amplifiers avoid continuous analog feedback, cutting area and power. However, they suffer AM-PM distortion—tiny timing delays in switching cause the output signal's phase to shift as amplitude changes, degrading linearity. This paper uses a polar switched-capacitor design with in-cell self-calibration: edge detectors on each unit cell measure switching delays, and a slope-to-phase tuner adjusts them in real time to compensate for phase shift, all within a single modulation period.
